speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to help me narrow down the cause, how long has this spinning sensation been happening, and does it worsen when you move your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of sudden-onset vertigo lasting approximately 3 minutes, occurring spontaneously or with minimal head movement, accompanied by nausea and vomiting, is highly characteristic of BPPV, likely due to a canalithiasis event. No further tests are required at this time.
